story.title: Brian Mazanec takes acting CISA infrastructure security role, bringing experience in cyber incident response and resilience - Industrial Cyber

facts.text: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has appointed Brian Bonacci to lead its emergency communications division and named Brian Mazanec acting executive assistant director for infrastructure security .
As acting EAD of CISA’s infrastructure security division, Mazanec will help lead the agency’s nationwide work to safeguard critical infrastructure against all hazards.
He will focus on risk management and resilience, partnering with members of the critical infrastructure community.

His work included directing responses to cyberattacks affecting the healthcare and public health sectors, including the 2024 Change Healthcare incident, as well as the 2026 hantavirus and Bundibugyo Ebola responses.
He also worked with CISA and the FBI on joint cybersecurity advisories and engaged critical infrastructure partners.
Butera succeeds Nick Andersen, who took over as acting CISA director after DHS named Gottumukkala its director of strategic implementation.
ExecutiveGov, published by Executive Mosaic, is a site dedicated to the news and headlines in the federal government.
ExecutiveGov serves as a news source for the hot topics and issues facing federal government departments and agencies such as Gov 2.0, cybersecurity policy, health IT, green IT and national security.
We also aim to spotlight various federal government employees and interview key government executives whose impact resonates beyond their agency.
Bonacci also spent nearly five years at Level 3 Communications, where he served multiple leadership positions spanning government advocacy, business operations and industry relations.
Mazanec was sworn in by CISA Acting Director Nick Andersen on Nov.

He will oversee CISA’s Infrastructure Security Division, which works with government and private-sector partners to identify vulnerabilities, manage risks, and improve resilience across the nation’s 16 critical infrastructure sectors.
Mazanec brings more than two decades of experience in risk assessment, critical infrastructure protection, and public-private coordination, CISA said.

At HHS, Mazanec helped direct the department’s response to major cybersecurity incidents affecting the healthcare sector, including the 2024 Change Healthcare ransomware attack, which disrupted healthcare operations nationwide, according to his CISA leadership biography .

Before joining HHS, Mazanec led the strategic warfare, security, and intelligence portfolio at the Government Accountability Office and worked on weapons of mass destruction issues at the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Nuclear Matters, and the Joint Staff.

Brian Mazanec, who previously oversaw health-sector preparedness at the Department of Health and Human Services, has been sworn in as acting executive assistant director for infrastructure security at CISA.
Mazanec was sworn in on Monday, according to CISA.
Mazanec's appointment coincides with CISA's launch of its critical infrastructure security and resilience month.

This year, the agency introduced the CI Fortify initiative, which encourages critical infrastructure organisations to remain resilient to successful cyber attacks and to plan for outages that could sever connections to internet, telecommunications and other technology services.
CISA has also been focused on securing defence critical infrastructure that supports military bases and operations, including through a partnership with the Army.
Mazanec most recently served as deputy assistant secretary and director of the Center for Preparedness within HHS's Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response.
He stepped down from that post last week after serving there since January 2023.
Earlier in his career, Mazanec led the strategic warfare, security and intelligence portfolio at the Government Accountability Office.
Christina Duvall has been named acting chief operations support officer.
Why it matters: The appointment places a health-sector cyber veteran in charge of securing all 16 critical infrastructure sectors across the United States.
